solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Make this with ice cream and use nuts (6)

indicatorNotes.nuts: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild

annotation.surface: A recipe card telling you to make something with ice cream and scatter nuts over it.
annotation.walkthrough: Nuts really do go on a sundae, so the surface reads as a topping instruction; "and use" looks like filler but is the whole fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A sundae is a dessert made with ice cream, so 'this' is exactly what you make with it.

entries.clue: Close family safeguarding son’s fur coat (8)

indicatorNotes.safeguarding: to safeguard is to hold something protectively, so SEAL KIN wraps round S

annotation.surface: A tight-knit family protecting a son's precious fur coat.
annotation.walkthrough: "Close family" reads as one phrase meaning near relatives; the first word is a verb here, not an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the pelt of the fur seal was long prized for coats, and the material's name stands for the garment.

entries.clue: Writer spreading lies on TV (8)

annotation.surface: A writer broadcasting falsehoods on television.
annotation.walkthrough: A novelist is a professional teller of untruths, which is what makes the surface sly.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: any author of fiction counts as a writer, and the surface's teller of lies fits the trade.

entries.clue: Roman courts held “in camera” trials (5)

indicatorNotes.held: the answer is held inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of camera and the start of trials

annotation.surface: Roman law courts sitting in private, behind closed doors.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all law courts, so "courts" sounds judicial; here they are open courtyards. In camera is legal Latin for a hearing held in private. The answer runs camer(A TRIA)ls.
annotation.definitionFit: An atrium was the open central court of a Roman house; atria is the plural.

entries.clue: Donning black uniform in time for breakfast (8)

annotation.definitionNote: 'in mourning' means wearing black; the answer names that state

indicatorNotes.in: the uniform letter goes in the time word

blocks.note: breakfast is eaten in the morning
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Someone putting on a black uniform at breakfast time.
annotation.walkthrough: "Black uniform" looks like one garment; black belongs to the definition and uniform is just its letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Mourning is the wearing of black clothes after a death.

entries.clue: Most talented new books (3,9)

annotation.definitionNote: the Old Testament is one collection made of many books

indicatorNotes.new: new makes the letters into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: A literary prize shortlist of the most gifted new books.
annotation.walkthrough: "New" sits beside "books", so the phrase looks like fresh publications; it makes an anagram of an answer that is anything but new, the joke being OLD from new.
annotation.definitionFit: The Old Testament is the first part of the Bible, a collection of books.

entries.clue: Swedes, maybe poor actors, not opening plays (4,5)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition gives one example; the answer is the class

indicatorNotes.not opening: the first letter of actors is not there

blocks.note: actors without its first letter A

annotation.surface: A review sneering that bad actors are keeping out of opening nights, with Swedes named as the culprits.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital S makes Swedes look like people from Sweden; a swede is also a root vegetable (rutabaga in the US). Poor looks like a critic's verdict but is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: The swede is a root crop, grown for its edible root.

entries.clue: High flyer’s current motors outside for all to see (6)

indicatorNotes.outside: the motors go outside the film-rating letter

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
U, 'universal', is the British film rating for all audiences

annotation.surface: An aviator's electric motors mounted on the outside where everyone can watch.
annotation.walkthrough: Icarus flew too near the sun on wax wings and fell, the original high flyer. The surface wants a modern aircraft with visible engines.
annotation.definitionFit: Icarus, of Greek myth, flew so high the sun melted his wings.

entries.clue: Water carrier in gallons, say (6)

annotation.surface: A container that holds water measured in gallons, for example.
annotation.walkthrough: "Water carrier" sounds like a bucket or tanker; it is the channel along a roof edge. "Say" looks like 'for example' but is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A gutter is a channel that carries rainwater away.

entries.clue: Part of speech bishop added on short notice (6)

indicatorNotes.short: short cuts the last letter off advert
indicatorNotes.added on: the bishop is added on at the end

blocks.note: an advert is a notice; short, it loses its T
B is bishop in chess notation

annotation.surface: A bishop giving a talk at short notice.
annotation.walkthrough: "Part of speech" sounds like an excerpt from the bishop's address; it is the grammar term. "Short notice" is a stock phrase split into a cut-down word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain grammar term: the traditional parts of speech include noun, verb and this word class that modifies verbs.

entries.clue: Champion! Finishing early to grab a drink (8)

indicatorNotes.Finishing early: the word finishes one letter early, losing its last letter
indicatorNotes.to grab: the cut word grabs the A, holding it inside

blocks.note: an advocate champions a cause; finishing early drops the final E

annotation.surface: A winner leaving the party early to go and grab a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark makes Champion a cheer; it is a verb-noun meaning supporter. Advocaat is a Dutch egg-and-brandy liqueur.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: this Dutch egg-yolk and brandy liqueur is one of many drinks.

entries.clue: An actor’s month playing London without underwear (6,6)

indicatorNotes.playing: the letters of London play about
indicatorNotes.without: without here means outside, so the jumbled London goes round the bra

blocks.note: MAR is the calendar abbreviation for March

annotation.surface: An actor spending a month on the London stage without any underwear.
annotation.walkthrough: "Without" reads as 'lacking', which fits the risqué surface; here it means outside, the old sense, so the bra ends up inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the star of On the Waterfront and The Godfather is one actor among many, hence 'An'.

entries.clue: Country fruit tree regularly pruned (9)

indicatorNotes.regularly pruned: pruning at regular intervals keeps every other letter

blocks.note: a sultana is a dried grape

annotation.surface: A gardening tip for a fruit tree out in the country, pruned at regular intervals.
annotation.walkthrough: "Country fruit tree" reads as a rural orchard; Country is a noun standing alone as the definition, and it means a nation ruled by a sultan.
annotation.definitionFit: A sultanate is a country ruled by a sultan, such as Oman or Brunei.

entries.clue: Reason why hearts murmured (5)

indicatorNotes.murmured: murmured means spoken quietly, so the answer is how the word sounds

blocks.note: the heart of an apple is its core

annotation.surface: An explanation of why a patient's heart has a murmur.
annotation.walkthrough: A heart murmur is a medical symptom, so the surface looks clinical. In a non-rhotic British accent, cores and cause sound the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what brings something about is the reason why it happened, the noun sense matching.

entries.clue: Fitting in with everyone in Victoria? (12)

indicatorNotes.in: everyone goes in the Victoria word

blocks.note: Victoria is a London railway station; the ? flags that it is one example

annotation.surface: Asking whether you would fit in with the crowd in Victoria, in Australia perhaps.
annotation.walkthrough: Victoria looks like the Australian state or a queen; it is the London terminus.
annotation.definitionFit: An installation is a fitting, something fitted in place.

entries.clue: Running in a circle around others (9)

indicatorNotes.around: the circle goes around the others word

annotation.surface: Someone jogging round a circuit, lapping everyone else.
annotation.walkthrough: "Running in a circle" looks like the whole picture; "Running in" is informal British for arresting, as a police officer runs a suspect in.
annotation.definitionFit: To run someone in is to arrest them.

entries.clue: Celebrated criminal finally charged (8)

indicatorNotes.finally: finally takes the last letter of criminal

blocks.note: an ionised atom carries an electric charge

annotation.surface: A famous crook finally brought to court.
annotation.walkthrough: "Charged" is a legal word in the surface; it is electrical in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past participle: made much of as a celebrity, treated like a lion of society.

entries.clue: Blood experts attempt to restrict nitrogen (8)

indicatorNotes.to restrict: the experts restrict nitrogen, closing round it

blocks.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

annotation.surface: Blood specialists trying to limit nitrogen in a sample.
annotation.walkthrough: "Blood experts" reads as one phrase, haematologists; Blood stands alone, in its sense of lineage.
annotation.definitionFit: Your blood, as in 'royal blood', is your ancestry.

entries.clue: Work on coaches, removing one set of gears (12)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, the work word comes on after the coaches word
indicatorNotes.removing one: one, the letter I, is taken out

blocks.note: coaches are railway carriages, TRAINS; lose I
a mission is a piece of work, an assignment

annotation.surface: Mechanics servicing buses and taking out one set of gears.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a bus garage, so coaches means buses; for the letters it means trains.
annotation.definitionFit: A vehicle's transmission is its gearbox and drive train.

entries.clue: Part of neck that is compressed by collar (6)

indicatorNotes.compressed: the phrase is squeezed into its short form
indicatorNotes.by: by means beside, so the collar goes next to it

blocks.note: sc. abbreviates the Latin scilicet, 'that is to say'
a ruff is a frilled collar

annotation.surface: A neck squeezed by a tight collar.
annotation.walkthrough: Most solvers know i.e. for "that is"; the Latin sc. means the same and is rarer. The surface is a tight shirt collar, which makes "compressed" look physical.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the loose skin at the back of the neck, by which a cat carries its kittens.

entries.clue: One snooker tool reduced, another free (6)

indicatorNotes.reduced: reduced cuts the last letter off rest

blocks.note: the rest supports a snooker cue; reduced, it loses T
the other snooker tool, the cue

annotation.surface: A snooker player getting one piece of kit cut down and another thrown in for nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: "Free" reads as costing nothing; it is a verb meaning set loose. In snooker the rest is a stick with a cross at the end for supporting the cue on long shots.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to save someone from danger or captivity is to set them free.

entries.clue: Aristocrat but not of the French game (5)

indicatorNotes.but not: the aristocrat but not the French word, which is removed

blocks.note: du is French for 'of the'; it is removed

annotation.surface: A noble who refuses to play a French game.
annotation.walkthrough: "Of the French game" reads as one phrase, like boules; the French part only tells you what to cut.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the board game of kings and pawns is one example of a game.

entries.clue: Phone receiver put to specific use (4-5)

blocks.note: to ring someone is to phone them
a fence is a receiver of stolen goods

annotation.surface: A telephone handset being used for one particular job.
annotation.walkthrough: "Phone receiver" is a handset; split, it is a call and a dealer in stolen goods.
annotation.definitionFit: To ring-fence money is to reserve it for one specific purpose.

entries.clue: Learner just possesses talent (5)

indicatorNotes.possesses: the just word possesses, holding the learner

annotation.surface: A beginner who simply has natural ability.
annotation.walkthrough: "Just" reads as 'simply'; it is the adjective meaning fair.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a natural aptitude, as in having a knack or gift for something.

entries.clue: With face scratched, uses ointments (8)

indicatorNotes.With face scratched: the face, the front letter, is scratched out

blocks.note: the uses of a thing are its functions; F goes

annotation.surface: Someone with a scratched face putting ointment on it.
annotation.walkthrough: "Uses" looks like the verb in the scene; it is a plural noun. Unction is an old word for ointment.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with an old flavour: oils and salves rubbed on the skin, as in the rite of anointing.

entries.clue: Dog bringing in first aid (6)

indicatorNotes.in first: the first letter of bringing goes in first

blocks.note: an asset is a help, an aid

annotation.surface: A rescue dog carrying in a first-aid kit.
annotation.walkthrough: "First aid" is a set phrase; break it, so first goes with bringing and aid stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: The basset is a short-legged hound.

entries.clue: Uplifting meals during which joy returns (8)

indicatorNotes.during which: the meals word holds the joy word, which happens during it
indicatorNotes.returns: the joy word comes back to front

annotation.surface: Cheering dinners at which happiness comes back.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a coherent picture of good food lifting spirits, so there's no hint that joy must be turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as adjectives: a film or story that lifts your mood is described with this compound.

entries.clue: Island resident’s fight to retain passport? (6)

indicatorNotes.to retain: the fight word retains the passport word inside

blocks.note: a passport is one form of ID; the ? marks the example

annotation.surface: An islander battling to keep hold of their passport.
annotation.walkthrough: Friday is Robinson Crusoe's companion on his desert island, Man Friday.
annotation.definitionFit: Man Friday lived on Crusoe's island, a resident there.
